newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-RIOS SENT PACKING BUT HENMAN WALTZES THROUGH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIOS SENT PACKING BUT HENMAN WALTZES THROUGH.

text.p: World number six Marcelo Rios of Chile, hampered by a leg injury, slumped to a 4-6 7-5 7-6 second-round defeat by Czech Martin Damm in the European Community tournament on Thursday, but said he would have forfeited the next round anyhow.
Sixth seed Tim Henman by contrast waltzed into the quarter-finals with an empathic 6-2 6-3 victory over Swede Mikael Tillstrom, recently recovered from 'flu.

"I'm not pleased because I lost. But I don't think I should have played. It was not a good decision to play," second-seeded Rios said. "I think that if I had won this match I would not have been able to play the next match."
Rios, 21, was forced to pull out of the Marseille final against Swede Thomas Enqvist last week but had come through the first round in Antwerp without mishap.

But Rios, the second seed and highest ranked player in the tournament following the withdrawal of top seed Goran Ivanisevic on Tuesday, was a pale shadow of the player who dominated Romanian Adrian Voinea in the first round.
Henman, Britain's brightest tennis star for two decades, said he felt more comfortable on court than in his first-round match against another Spanish player, Sergi Bruguera.

"I definitely served better and took opportunities from the baseline with my forehand," said Henman, who became the first seeded player to gain access to the quarter-finals where he meets Spaniard Francisco Clavet.

Six other seeds, including the top four, pulled out or were knocked out. Fifth seed Felix Mantilla, due on court against Belgian Dick Norman later on Thursday, is the only other seeded player still in the running.
"I think I'm going to be the one dictating the points...most of the time he is going to stay behind the baseline so I have to be aggressive but also patient," Henman said about Clavet.

Rios, who had never played Damm before, faded as the match progressed. In the final set he quickly fell 5-2 behind but battled back to level 6-6, more because of Damm's erratic play than through his own performance.
Damm, world number 48, twisted his ankle when leading 6-5 and had it strapped before resuming play.
The decisive tie-break was a sad affair with Rios clearly holding back and the match was sealed 7-3.

"I didn't feel good enough to play well. With every point I was killing my leg," said Rios, wo will take next week off and travel to the United States to have his leg treated, partly with ultra-sound massage.

Belgian lucky loser Filip Dewulf, who was called up only late on Tuesday after top seed Goran Ivanisevic pulled out with shoulder tendinitis, saved three set points in the first-set tiebreak before beating Frenchman Cedric Pioline 7-6 6-4.
